name: Kansas
note: In Kansas the funeral director who first takes custody must file the death certificate through the Kansas electronic death registration system (KS-EDRS) within three days, before burial or removal from the state. The cause-of-death certifier or the coroner completes the medical part in the same system, and every cremation needs a coroner's permit. The state registrar sends a monthly list of deceased adult residents to each county election officer and district court clerk, and may give fact-of-death data to benefit agencies. Election officers must also remove voters on the strength of a newspaper or funeral-home obituary.

citations.title: Determination of death
citations.quote: A determination of death must be made in accordance with accepted medical standards.

citations.title: Notification of death to coroner or deputy, when
citations.quote: shall be notified by the physician in attendance, by any law enforcement officer, by the embalmer

citations.title: Definitions -- cause of death certifier
citations.quote: "Cause of death certifier" means a person licensed to practice medicine and surgery by the state board of healing arts, a physician assistant

citations.title: Registration of deaths and stillbirths
citations.quote: shall be filed with the state registrar within three days after such death and prior to removal of the body from the state

citations.title: Registration of deaths -- funeral director files
citations.quote: The funeral director or person acting as such who first assumes custody of a dead body shall file the death certificate.

citations.title: Registration of deaths -- certification of cause
citations.quote: shall obtain the certification of cause of death from the cause of death certifier who was last in attendance prior to burial

citations.title: Registration of deaths -- funeral director verification form
citations.quote: any such form, verified within 21 days of date of death, shall be prima facie evidence of the facts pertaining to establishing such death

citations.title: Registration of deaths -- coroner certification
citations.quote: shall complete and sign the certification of cause of death within 24 hours after receipt of the death certificate

citations.title: Registration of deaths -- filing before disposal
citations.quote: In every instance a certificate shall be filed prior to interment or disposal of the body.

citations.title: Registration of deaths -- Kansas electronic death registration system
citations.quote: shall be filed through the Kansas electronic death registration system maintained by the Kansas department of health and environment

citations.title: Delayed determination of cause of death
citations.quote: If the cause of death cannot be determined within three days, the certification of the cause of death may be filed as pending.

citations.title: Certified copies or abstracts
citations.quote: the state registrar shall, upon request, furnish to any applicant a certified copy or a certified abstract of any certificate, or any part thereof.

citations.title: Disclosure of records -- direct interest
citations.quote: has a direct interest in the matter recorded and the information contained in the record is necessary for the determination of personal or property rights

citations.title: Disclosure of records -- release to agencies
citations.quote: the secretary may direct the state registrar to release birth, death and stillbirth certificate data to federal, state or municipal agencies

citations.title: Monthly reports of deceased residents to county election officers
citations.quote: On or before the 20th day of each month, the state registrar shall furnish to the county election officer of each county

citations.title: Monthly reports of deceased residents -- clerks of the district court
citations.quote: by the clerk of the district court in each county for the purpose of correcting juror information for such county

citations.title: Fact of death information to benefit programs
citations.quote: Fact of death information may be disseminated to state and federal agencies administering benefit programs. Such information shall be used for file clearance purposes only.

citations.title: Authorization for cremation; permit to cremate
citations.quote: shall be cremated unless a coroner's permit to cremate has been executed to authorize such cremation

citations.title: Crimes, prosecution, penalties
citations.quote: neglects or refuses to perform any of the duties imposed upon such person by this act, shall be fined not more than $200

citations.title: Removal of names of voters -- state list of deceased residents
citations.quote: appears on a list of deceased residents compiled by the secretary of health and environment as provided in K.S.A. 65-2422

citations.title: Removal of names of voters -- online funeral-home obituary
citations.quote: an obituary notice published online by a funeral home located in the county reports the death of such registered voter

steps.title: Death determined under accepted medical standards
steps.who: Not specified by statute; a determination under accepted medical standards (in practice a physician or other licensed practitioner).
steps.summary: Kansas has the Uniform Determination of Death Act standard (irreversible cessation of circulatory and respiratory functions, or of all brain functions), but no statute read names who may pronounce.

steps.title: Reportable deaths notified to the district coroner
steps.who: The physician in attendance, any law enforcement officer, the embalmer, or any other person.
steps.trigger: Death by violence, unlawful means, suicide or casualty; sudden death in apparent health; death not regularly attended by a physician; suspicious death; death in custody; certain child deaths; or public interest.
steps.summary: The coroner of the county of death is notified, and the coroner of the county where the cause arose decides whether to investigate. A child's death must be reported to the coroner immediately.

steps.title: Next of kin supplies personal data
steps.who: The next of kin or the best qualified person or source available.
steps.summary: The funeral director obtains the decedent's personal data from the next of kin.

steps.title: Cause of death certifier completes the medical certification
steps.who: The cause of death certifier last in attendance: a physician, physician assistant or APRN (or a coroner).

deadline.text: within the three-day filing period; may be filed as pending

steps.summary: The certification goes through the Kansas electronic death registration system. If cause cannot be determined within three days it is filed as pending and reported later.

steps.title: Coroner certifies unattended or medicolegal deaths
steps.who: The district coroner, deputy coroner or special deputy coroner.
steps.trigger: Death without medical attendance, or one requiring postmortem inquiry.

deadline.text: within 24 hours after receipt of the death certificate

steps.summary: The coroner investigates and signs the certification of cause, or files it as pending.

steps.title: Funeral director files the death certificate through KS-EDRS
steps.who: The funeral director or person acting as such who first assumes custody of the body.

deadline.text: within three days after death, before interment or disposal and before removal from the state

steps.summary: The certificate is filed with the state registrar (KDHE) through the Kansas electronic death registration system and registered when complete; the filed certificate is the official death record. Neglecting a duty under the act carries a fine of up to $200.

steps.title: Coroner's permit required before cremation
steps.trigger: Intended cremation of a body whose death or cause of death occurred in Kansas.
steps.summary: No body may be cremated without an executed coroner's permit; an electronic or faxed signed copy is sufficient.

steps.title: Certified copies to applicants with a direct interest
steps.who: The state registrar (KDHE Office of Vital Statistics).
steps.summary: The state registrar issues a certified copy or abstract only to an applicant with a direct interest whose personal or property rights depend on the record; the decision can be reviewed by the secretary or a court.

steps.title: Funeral director's verified death form as prima facie evidence
steps.who: A licensed Kansas funeral director, on a form bought from the state registrar.
steps.trigger: A family's need for proof of death before certified copies are available.

deadline.text: verified within 21 days of the date of death

steps.summary: Besides the official certificate, a funeral director may verify the death particulars on a KDHE form. Verified within 21 days, it is prima facie evidence of the death and costs the same as a certified copy.

steps.title: Monthly list of deceased residents to county election officers
steps.who: The state registrar, to the county election officer of each county.
steps.trigger: Death certificates filed in the preceding month for residents aged 18 or over.

deadline.text: on or before the 20th day of each month

steps.summary: The state registrar sends each county, free of charge, the name, age or date of birth, address and date of death of deceased adult residents. The election officer must remove anyone on the list from the registration books and party affiliation lists.

steps.title: Same monthly list to clerks of the district court for juror records
steps.who: The state registrar, to the clerk of the district court in each county.

deadline.text: on or before the 20th day of each month

steps.summary: The monthly deceased-residents list also goes to district court clerks, confidentially, to correct juror information.

steps.title: A funeral home's online obituary triggers voter removal
steps.who: The county election officer, acting on a newspaper obituary or an online obituary published by a funeral home in the county.
steps.summary: Kansas makes a published obituary, including one posted online by a local funeral home, a ground the election officer must act on to remove the voter. No registry data is needed.

steps.title: Fact-of-death data to benefit programs
steps.who: The state registrar, at the secretary's direction, for state and federal agencies administering benefit programs (and other federal, state or municipal agencies).
steps.summary: Fact-of-death information may be given to benefit-paying agencies, for file clearance only, and the secretary may direct release of death-certificate data to other agencies.

steps.title: Private bodies rely on certified copies or the funeral director's verified form
steps.who: Next of kin or the estate's representative.
steps.trigger: Need to prove the death to a bank, insurer or other private body.
steps.summary: State law gives private bodies no death feed or verification service: copies need a direct interest tied to personal or property rights. In practice the family presents a certified copy or the funeral director's verified form.

registrationDeadlineDays.note: Three days after death, before interment or disposal and before removal from the state.

informantDuty.note: The funeral director or person acting as such who first takes custody files the certificate.

medicalExaminerScrutiny.note: No independent review of every certificate. The coroner certifies only unattended or medicolegal deaths, but must issue a permit before every cremation.

electronicRegistration.note: All death certificates and cause-of-death certifications must be filed through the Kansas electronic death registration system.

centralPopulationRegister.note: No population register; the death certificate filed with the state registrar is the official death record.

governmentPropagation.note: Under state law, a monthly list goes to every county election officer and district court clerk, and fact-of-death data may go to benefit agencies. No statutory death feed to the Division of Vehicles or the Department of Revenue's tax side was found. Federal feeds such as SSA are in us-federal.

certificateAccess.note: Direct interest required, and the information must be necessary to determine personal or property rights.

gaps: Who may pronounce death is not set out in the statutes read (K.S.A. 77-205 sets only the standard); no nurse-pronouncement statute was located in the ch. 65 catchlines.

K.S.A. 25-2316c(f)(2)(E) cross-refers to 'K.S.A. 65-2422' for the deceased-residents list, but the list duty is now in § 65-2422d(f) (the revisor notes the two versions); both are recorded as one route.

No statute was found requiring KDHE to notify the Division of Vehicles (driver licences), the Department of Revenue or KanCare (Medicaid) of deaths. Kansas has no full-text statute search, so this is a negative from catchlines and the sections read, not the whole code.
Kansas Administrative Regulations (K.A.R. 28-17, vital statistics) were not read.

privateSectorVerification is deliberately left out of this file so that the us-federal value (LADMF/SSA) applies in the viewer. State law gives private bodies no route beyond certified copies and the funeral director's verified form.
Probate notice to creditors (public stage) was not researched.
